sam: Spinning up SJC GPUs. Need a quick network/egress design + cost sanity check before we hand off to oncall. High level: TGW transit in infra-account, shared NAT in transit VPC, private Route53 delegation for service DNS. Questions: routing tables, SNAT behavior, DNS resolver setup, and an egress cost estimate. Attaching sketch: https://drive.redwood/sjc-egress-sketch (public within org). CC @maya @jordan @nina

maya: Ack. Quick ask: what CIDR ranges and which AZs are you planning to use? Also expected egress baseline and peak — that'll drive NAT sizing/costs.

sam: Details below — plan is 3 AZs (sjc-1,sjc-2,sjc-3). CIDRs: `10.72.0.0/22` (control plane), `10.72.4.0/21` (gpu compute). Transit VPC: `10.200.0.0/16`. Expected steady egress ~8Gbps, occasional bursts up to 40Gbps (training sync, checkpoint pushes). Monthly data egress estimate ~25TB (initial), potential to grow.

jordan: Notes from network side: prefer central NAT (managed NAT GW) in transit VPC behind TGW. Route tables per spoke VPC should have default `0.0.0.0/0` -> TGW attachment (propagated). Then TGW route to NAT subnet in transit. If we used NAT instances we'd need to disable source-dest check. Managed NAT GW simpler at this scale but watch costs for data processing. Also plan for TGW attachments across AZs to avoid asymmetric routing if an AZ NAT fails.

nina: Cost quick math (rough): managed NAT GW: ~$0.045/hour per NAT GW * 3 AZs => ~ $9.72/day. Data processing: ~$0.045/GB (example, adjust for cloud provider) -> ~25TB * 1024 GB * $0.045 ~= $1152/mo. TGW/hour attachments & data processing add ~$300/mo. So ballpark extra egress network cost ~ $1.5k/mo. If bursts to 40TB/month, add linear proportion. I'll run precise numbers for SJC rates.

sam: Thanks. Can someone write a short validation checklist we can run post-provisioning (smoke tests + what to measure during handoff)? I want a concise runbook for the oncall owner.

maya: Draft checklist (will push into docs):
- Pre-check: confirm VPC CIDRs and TGW attachments: `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateways` / `aws ec2 describe-vpc-attachments`
- Routing: from a gpu instance: `ip route get 8.8.8.8` should show next-hop = local gw -> TGW -> NAT (no direct IGW)
- NAT SNAT: `curl -sS http://ifconfig.me` from instance -> ensure public SNAT IP is one of the transit NAT GWs
- DNS: `dig @<resolver-ip> internal.service.svc +short` should resolve to private IPs; `dig external.com` should work via forwarders
- Trace: `traceroute -n 1.1.1.1` validate path goes via transit NAT subnets
- Bandwidth: `iperf3` test between a test pod and a public ip to ensure expected throughput; baseline p50/p99
- BGP/Peering (if applicable): validate routes learned and no overlaps
- Packet loss/latency smoke: pings to control plane & to an external endpoint; loss <0.1% expected
- Cost sanity: confirm Cloud billing alerts exist for egress > 30TB/month and NAT GW alarms for >70% utilization (custom metric)
- Rollback plan: detach TGW route, fall back to per-VPC NAT (if configured)

jordan: Add network-specific commands: `aws ec2 get-transit-gateway-route-table --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-xyz` and check `State == active` for routes to NAT subnets. Also confirm `AutoAcceptSharedAttachments` behavior if sharing across accounts.

ops-bot: smoke-tests/sjc-egress 1912350400 SUCCESS - low-level validation suite passed (route propagation, dig/resolver check, sample iperf).

sam: Nice, ops-bot. Jordan — DNS specifics? We need private hosted zones per environment and conditional forwarders for the resolver endpoints?

jordan: Prefer: create private hosted zone in transit account, then associate spoke VPCs. Use Route53 Resolver endpoints (inbound/outbound) for split-horizon and for forwarding to corporate resolvers. For cross-account, use resolver rules with rule-association to VPCs rather than delegating NS records (simpler to manage). Also remember to create Resolver endpoints in at least 2 AZs for HA.

nina: I'll include DNS resolver charges in the cost doc. Resolver endpoint hourly + outbound endpoints data processing similar to NAT costs.

sam: Handoff plan: schedule to hand off to oncall (liam) next Thursday 09:00 PT. Oncall will run the checklist and we will monitor for 24h. @liam can you take validation and initial watch?

liam: ack. I'll run the post-handoff checklist and verify: BGP paths, p95 latency to model endpoints, packet loss, and billing spikes. If anything looks off, escalate to eng-infra pager.

maya: I'll own the cost runbook and post concrete monthly numbers + alert thresholds to the docs page by EOD tomorrow. I'll also add Terraform snippets showing TGW routes and `aws_route` examples.

sam: Great — next actions: (1) maya posts cost doc + TF snippet, (2) jordan prepares DNS + TGW route docs, (3) nina finalizes cost numbers and creates billing alerts, (4) liam will own handoff validation. I'll kick off infra provisioning now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
